name: Exchange a runner key for a token
description: The only unauthenticated runner route, and the only one that ever sees the long-lived key: it is presented once every ten minutes to one route and never accompanies a match write, so the credential that can finish a match is the short-lived one. A RUNNER SELF-REGISTERS RATHER THAN BEING ENROLLED -- the upsert on (key_id, label) means 'start a runner' is copy the key and run the image, and a second machine on the same key is simply a second row. The upsert deliberately does NOT clear revoked_at: a revoked runner may keep announcing itself, and it keeps being refused, because resurrection by reconnection would make revocation advisory. Refusals are 401 for a key that matches no live admin's live key and 409 for a node whose ops_budget disagrees with the season -- the second is a misconfiguration check and is worth exactly that, because with trusted operators misconfiguration is what actually happens. ITS RATE LIMIT IS A CEILING ON MACHINES PER SOURCE ADDRESS, and has to be: this is the route that establishes the principal, so the limit cannot be keyed on one, and several machines in one office are one address. The token is also minted far more often than its ten-minute life suggests -- every cron run is a fresh execution carrying no state, so each mints one and uses it once: measured, 214 exchanges against 214 authenticated calls in 120s, 0.89/s per idle runner. At the 5 rps this shipped with, the sixth machine behind a NAT was refused, SILENTLY: the caller's call is soft, data.tok.token stays unset, the run ends at `noauth` with outcome no_token, and the channel traces errors_only -- so it claims nothing and looks healthy. Hence runner_token_rate, equal to runner_rate: an exchange is no dearer than the claim it precedes, and a 32-byte random key is no brute-force surface at 30 rps. The real repair is not minting a ten-minute credential for one call. Until then the only symptom is last_seen_at ceasing to move, since this route stamps it.

with.name: A runner names itself
with.description: The label is the machine's own name and is half the upsert key, so it is required rather than defaulted: a runner that did not say which machine it is would take over another one's row.

tasks.name: Register this runner
tasks.description: An invalid key matches no row and writes nothing, so the refusal needs no separate lookup and this statement never has to branch on whether the key existed. The JOIN to a live admin is inside the statement rather than in a guard task -- a JSONLogic guard fails OPEN if it is ever wrong, and a JOIN cannot be forgotten.

tasks.name: Read the runner back
tasks.description: Through live_runners, so a revoked key, a revoked runner, a deleted user or an admin who is no longer one all answer nothing here -- the same read the eight match statements make, asked once at the door. ops_required is the tightest adapter_ops_max any live season declares; a deployment running one game has exactly one.

with.name: No live runner
with.description: One answer for a key that never existed, a key that was revoked, a runner that was revoked and an owner who is no longer an admin. They are one refusal on purpose: telling them apart would tell an anonymous caller which keys are real.

with.name: The node's budget is not the season's
with.description: engine.ops_budget is Orion INSTANCE config and cannot ride the claim response the way turn_ms does, so it is self-reported and checked here. A node admitted under one ceiling and playing under another strikes seats for a rule nobody wrote down; refusing the token is how that becomes a message instead of a mystery.

input.query: UPDATE runner_keys SET last_used_at = now() WHERE key_hash = ($1)::text

tasks.name: Tell the key's admin a runner is on the wrong engine
tasks.description: A runner whose engine_digest no live season pins claims nothing, for ever, and looks healthy doing it: it calls in, mints tokens, and the claim answers idle. So the exchange -- the one call that carries the digest -- tells the admin who holds the key, once per runner per digest (the key), and only while some season is live, because with none live every runner is idle for a reason that is not theirs. A mismatch is not refused: the admin may be rolling the fleet ahead of a season that has not opened. continue_on_error, because a notification must never cost a runner its token.

tasks.name: Mint the runner token
tasks.description: TEN MINUTES, and the audience is what separates the two token families: aud 'runner' signed with RUNNER_TOKEN_SECRET, browser sessions signed with SOMA_SESSION_SECRET and carrying no audience at all, so a stolen cookie is not a runner and a stolen runner token is not a sign-in. The key id travels as a claim rather than as a `kid` header, because the verifying side lists one unnamed key and header routing would look for a key id that is not there. Expiry is not the revocation mechanism -- live_runners is -- it is the bound on how long a leaked token is worth anything.
